newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks jump on good news from manufacturing sector.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks jump on good news from manufacturing sector.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks posted strong gains Tuesday as a drop in a key measure of manufacturing activity soothed Wall Street's fears of an over-heating economy on the same day that the Federal Reserve was weighing monetary policy.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 54.06 points at 7,726.85.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 15-10 on active volume of 311 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The rally was ignited by the National Association of Purchasing Management report that its June index of activity showed growth in the manufacturing sector slowed in June from a month earlier, with an accompanying drop in prices.

The index dropped to 55.7 percent in June from 57.1 percent in May. Its Production Index decreased from 57.0 percent to 56.0 percent and its New Orders Index declined from 64.2 percent to 62.0 percent.
The lower reading calmed fears that excessive growth in the manufacturing sector might fuel inflation, analysts said.
While blue-chip stocks flourished, the technology and small-name stocks lagged amid profit warnings heading into the official start next week of the earnings reporting period.
"The market has a nice tone to it," said Frank Calta, managing director of institutional trading at Dain Bosworth.
"Everybody is watching the Fed, nobody expects any action from them and we should be holding steady here," he said.
Financial markets were susceptible to inflation and interest rate jitters as the Fed interest-rate-setting group began a two-day meeting, which will end Wednesday afternoon.

"Two NAPM components -- the prices index and the supplier deliveries index -- considered to be leading indicators of inflation and are closely watched by the Fed, declined," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
"This is very encouraging for bonds and the Fed," he said.
The bond market rose, with the 30-year Treasury bond up 16/32, lowering its yield to 6.75 percent from 6.79 percent on Monday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Analysts also said stocks normally get a boost heading into a patriotic holiday, such as the July 4 Independence Day.
"Historically, the bias of the market has been higher when faced with a flag-waving holiday," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
But he said trading activity would thin going into the holiday weekend, preceded by Thursday's June employment report.
The stocks of larger companies, particularly drugmakers and financial services providers, led the broader market higher, but technology stocks were not participating.
The Nasdaq composite, heavily weighted with technology firms, was down 4.57 points at 1,436.50.
"It's all of the earnings warnings from tech firms and the proverbial summer slowdown," Bleier said.

Cyrix Corp. lost 1-3/4 to 19-5/8 after forecasting a second-quarter loss due to weak demand and price pressures for its older-generation microprocessors. Rival chipmaker Intel Corp. was down 2-5/16 at 139-1/2 in active trading.

Among other issues, office supply company Office Depot Inc. fell 3-13/16 to 15-5/8, after a federal judge dealt a potentially fatal blow Monday to its planned $4.6 billion merger with Staples Inc. Staples was up 1-1/8 at 24-3/8.
